digest.component_or_area: Git fetch coordination in rebar store and snapshot paths
propositions: Parallel Git fetches updating remote-tracking refs in a shared common directory race without coordination, causing stale-reference CAS failures where a ref is at an unexpected value
The sync path fetch runs outside the store write lock before line 304 and the snapshot path uses a snapshot-store-specific lock, but neither coordinates with each other or with concurrent operations
Deterministic controlled experiments confirm 82/128 parallel fetches fail with CAS mismatch while 128/128 serialized fetches succeed, proving the mechanism

Bounded retry of CAS-mismatch failures combined with a cross-process fetch-coordination lock keyed on the canonical Git common directory resolves the race while preserving the requirement that network I/O does not hold the ticket write lock

Non-rebar Git processes sharing the common directory can still cause residual CAS races; retry is bounded and sync treats exhaustion as best-effort skip while snapshot fails closed with actionable error
